title: ARM templates and Bicep: read, modify, deploy, export and convert
learningObjective: Read and change ARM JSON and Bicep files. Deploy them safely with validate and what-if. Pick the right deployment mode. Export or convert existing infrastructure.
foundation: Infrastructure as code means describing Azure resources in a file, so you can deploy the same environment again and again without clicking through the portal.
Azure Resource Manager (ARM) templates are JSON files. Bicep is a simpler language for the same thing: it is converted into ARM JSON before deployment.
A template has parameters (values you supply at deployment, such as a VM name), variables (values it calculates), resources (what to create) and outputs (values it returns).
Deployments are declarative: you say what you want, and ARM works out the order and creates or updates resources to match.
engineer: The parts of an ARM JSON file: $schema and contentVersion, the header; parameters, values you pass in; variables, values the file works out; functions, your own helpers; resources, what to create; outputs, values it gives back.
Parameter options: type; defaultValue; allowedValues; minValue and maxValue; metadata (a description). Use secureString or secureObject for secrets, so they aren't shown or logged.
Each resource has: type; apiVersion; name; location; properties; and, when needed, dependsOn (create after another resource), copy (create several), condition (create only if true).

Template functions to know: resourceId() builds a resource's ID; reference() reads a deployed resource's values; concat() and format() join text; uniqueString() makes a repeatable unique name; resourceGroup().location gives the resource group's region.

The same thing in Bicep: param, with decorators such as @secure(), @allowed() and @minLength(); var; resource symbolicName 'type@apiVersion' = {...}; module, to reuse another file; output; existing, to point at a resource that's already there; for loops and if conditions.
Dependencies in Bicep: when one resource uses another's symbolic name (for example vnet.id), Bicep knows to create that one first. You rarely need dependsOn.
Converting: az bicep build turns Bicep into JSON. az bicep decompile turns JSON into Bicep, but the result may need tidying.

Order of creation: ARM creates resources in parallel unless a dependency says otherwise. A missing dependency gives random 'not found' errors. Two resources depending on each other (circular) fail validation.
Where you can deploy: resource group (az deployment group create); subscription (az deployment sub create), for example to create resource groups or assign policy; management group; tenant.
Passing parameters: on the command line; from a .parameters.json file; from a .bicepparam file. Secrets can come from Key Vault references.

Deployment modes: Incremental, the default, adds and updates what's in the file and leaves everything else alone; Complete deletes anything in the resource group that's not in the file (resource group deployments only).

Check before you deploy: az deployment group validate checks the file. az deployment group what-if shows what will be created, changed or deleted. Always run what-if before Complete mode or a risky change.

Getting a template from what exists: 'Export template' on a resource group captures what's there now, but with fixed values, and some types can't be exported. The Deployments page keeps the exact file and parameters of every past deployment.
Sharing templates: publish them as template specs. Others can deploy them, and you control who with RBAC.

animation.caption: Edit a template's dependencies and parameters, deploy in Incremental or Complete mode, and export/decompile.

example.title: Changing a network through a template
body: The platform team keeps network.bicep in Git. A pull request changes a subnet's address range. The pipeline runs az deployment group what-if. It shows one change (Modify) to the subnet and nothing deleted.

After approval, the pipeline deploys in Incremental mode, using one .bicepparam file for dev and one for prod. An old storage account someone made by hand in the same resource group is left alone, because Complete mode isn't used.

prerequisites: Azure CLI with Bicep (az bicep install), or Azure PowerShell
The target resource group or subscription
permissions: Microsoft.Resources/deployments/* at the target level (Contributor or Owner)
Permission for every resource type in the file
limits: Template size 4 MB; 256 parameters; 800 resources per deployment
Deployment history keeps up to 800 deployments per resource group (older ones are deleted automatically)
Complete mode only for resource group deployments
portal: Deploy a custom template > Build your own template in the editor, or load a quickstart.
Resource group > Deployments: view history, inputs, outputs and the template; redeploy.
Resource group > Automation > Export template: download or save to the template library.
Template specs: create and version reusable templates.
configuration.cli:
az deployment group validate -g rg-app --template-file main.bicep --parameters main.bicepparam
az deployment group what-if -g rg-app --template-file main.bicep --parameters main.bicepparam
az deployment group create -g rg-app --template-file main.bicep --parameters main.bicepparam
az deployment group create -g rg-app --template-file main.json --parameters @main.parameters.json --mode Complete
az group export --name rg-app > exported.json
az bicep decompile --file exported.json
az bicep build --file main.bicep
az deployment group export -g rg-app --name main
configuration.powershell:
Test-AzResourceGroupDeployment -ResourceGroupName rg-app -TemplateFile main.bicep -TemplateParameterFile main.parameters.json
New-AzResourceGroupDeployment -ResourceGroupName rg-app -TemplateFile main.bicep -TemplateParameterFile main.parameters.json -WhatIf
New-AzResourceGroupDeployment -ResourceGroupName rg-app -TemplateFile main.bicep -TemplateParameterFile main.parameters.json -Mode Incremental
Export-AzResourceGroup -ResourceGroupName rg-app -Path .\exported.json
Save-AzResourceGroupDeploymentTemplate -ResourceGroupName rg-app -DeploymentName main

lab.objective: Deploy a template, fix dependency and parameter errors, and understand what Complete mode deletes.
steps: Run the default Bicep deployment and read the deployment waves.
Apply 'Missing dependency', then 'Circular dependency' and 'Parameter not in allowedValues'. Read each failure.
Open Incremental vs Complete. Compare what happens to stlegacy, with and without a lock.
Open Export and convert. Export, then decompile.
expected: Validation errors for cycles and allowedValues
Complete mode deletes stlegacy unless locked
lab.cost: None. The simulation runs entirely in the browser.

troubleshooting.cause: Two resources depend on each other, directly or through others.
troubleshooting.fix: Remove the dependency you don't need, or split the file into modules.

troubleshooting.symptom: ResourceNotFound for a subnet during deployment, but it works when you retry.
troubleshooting.cause: A missing dependency, so ARM sometimes creates things in the wrong order.
troubleshooting.fix: In Bicep, use the VNet's symbolic name. In JSON, add dependsOn with resourceId().

troubleshooting.symptom: A deployment deleted resources you didn't expect.
troubleshooting.cause: Complete mode removed everything not in the file.
troubleshooting.fix: Use Incremental, or run what-if first. Protect key resources with locks.

troubleshooting.symptom: An exported template fails when you deploy it again.
troubleshooting.cause: It has fixed values and read-only properties, and may be missing types that can't be exported.
troubleshooting.fix: Clean it up and add parameters, or start from the deployment history or a quickstart template.

comparisons.difference: Works across clouds and keeps a state file. ARM and Bicep have no state file; Azure itself is the record of what exists.
AWS's template language (JSON or YAML). A CloudFormation stack is like an Azure deployment plus a deployment stack.

misconceptions.myth: Bicep is deployed by a separate Bicep service.
misconceptions.reality: No. Bicep is turned into ARM JSON, and ARM deploys it.

misconceptions.myth: Incremental mode deletes resources you removed from the file.
misconceptions.reality: No. Only Complete mode deletes them.
No. Using another resource's symbolic name creates the dependency for you.

architectureDecisions: Write Bicep, keep it in Git, deploy through a pipeline: and run what-if every time.
Reuse with modules and template specs: modules for building blocks, template specs to share them with other teams.
Keep secrets out of parameter files: use @secure() and Key Vault references.

walkthrough.subtitle: Describe your infrastructure in a file, and let Azure build it the same way every time.

steps.label: Click-ops
steps.title: Building the same environment by hand, again
body: Dev, test and production should be identical. Clicking through the portal three times guarantees small differences.

steps.label: ARM JSON
steps.title: An ARM template is a JSON description
body: Sections: $schema and contentVersion; parameters (values you supply at deploy time); variables (values worked out inside); resources (what to create, with type, apiVersion, name, location and properties); outputs (values returned).
Functions like [parameters('name')] and [resourceGroup().location] fill in values.

steps.label: Bicep
steps.title: Bicep says the same thing more simply
body: Bicep is a cleaner language for the same templates: param, var, resource and output keywords, no brackets and quotes everywhere. It is converted to ARM JSON when you deploy.

callout.text: On the exam, read templates calmly: find the parameter, follow where it is used, and check the resource type and SKU.

steps.label: Deploy
steps.title: Deploy, preview and choose a mode
body: Deploy with the portal (Deploy a custom template), az deployment group create, or New-AzResourceGroupDeployment. Use what-if to preview changes.
Incremental mode (default) adds and updates, leaving other resources alone. Complete mode deletes resources in the group that are not in the template.

callout.text: Complete mode can delete resources you forgot to put in the template.

steps.label: Export
steps.title: Start from what already exists
body: Export template (resource group or resource > Automation > Export template) produces ARM JSON from deployed resources. az bicep decompile converts that JSON into a Bicep file. Clean it up and add parameters before reusing it.

steps.label: Recap
steps.title: Templates
body: Write it once, deploy it many times.
recap: Export template, then az bicep decompile

handsOn.title: Deploy a storage account from a Bicep file, then export it
handsOn.cost: Cents for one empty storage account.
before: Signed in at portal.azure.com as Owner of a subscription (a free or pay-as-you-go account works). Work in a resource group called rg-az104-lab.
If rg-az104-lab does not exist yet: search 'Resource groups' > Create > name rg-az104-lab, region UAE North (or any region near you) > Review + create > Create.

steps.do: Cloud Shell: select the >_ icon at the top of the portal, choose Bash, and 'No storage account required' if asked.
Paste the whole box below into Cloud Shell and press Enter. It creates the file main.bicep.
steps.see: No output. Check the file with: cat main.bicep
steps.code:
cat > main.bicep <<'EOF'
param name string
param location string = resourceGroup().location
resource sa 'Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts@2023-05-01' = {
  name: name
  location: location
  sku: { name: 'Standard_LRS' }
  kind: 'StorageV2'
}
output id string = sa.id
EOF

steps.do: Preview: az deployment group what-if -g rg-az104-lab --template-file main.bicep --parameters name=st<yourinitials>bicep1
steps.see: A list showing one resource to Create (+).

steps.do: Deploy: az deployment group create -g rg-az104-lab --template-file main.bicep --parameters name=st<yourinitials>bicep1
steps.see: JSON output with provisioningState: Succeeded and the id output.

steps.do: In the portal open rg-az104-lab > Settings > Deployments.
steps.see: The 'main' deployment with its inputs, outputs and the template used.
An ARM JSON template describing everything in the group. Select Download.

steps.do: Back in Cloud Shell, export the group to JSON and convert it to Bicep:
steps.see: A new file exported.bicep. Read it with: cat exported.bicep
steps.code:
az group export -n rg-az104-lab > exported.json
az bicep decompile --file exported.json

check: The storage account was created by your Bicep file.
You have an exported template and a decompiled Bicep file.
cleanup: When you finish for the day: Resource groups > rg-az104-lab > Delete resource group > type the name > Delete. This removes everything inside it.
